label: three_state_target_trap_profiles_v4
purpose: Define controlled BEC, SSP and ID imaging objects on the finite-temperature core scale obtained from the original Oxford Trap III frequencies in the dissertation B-parallel-k geometry.

source_morphology.peak_count_boundary: Three dominant peaks describe the selected source morphologies; the source phase diagram contains other peak counts as atom number and scattering length change.
source_morphology.spacing_boundary: The Chomaz et al. supplementary analysis explicitly uses d = 2.8 um as the mean droplet separation representative of its 166Er experiment and corresponding supersolid calculations. The imaging model adopts that reported Er scale; it is not a roton wavelength recalculated for Trap III.
source_morphology.evidence_boundary: The source supplies the morphology classes, representative scattering lengths and the 2.8 um Er droplet-separation scale. It does not fix the target finite-temperature population, analytic peak weights and widths, or two-dimensional density arrays.

target_scale_anchor.orientation_boundary: Trap III frequencies are reused, while the dissertation retains B parallel k parallel x rather than reproducing the source field orientation.
target_scale_anchor.selection: retain the measured Oxford total atom number and temperature; recalculate the finite-temperature core in Trap III under the dissertation orientation

construction_boundary.generated_truth_role: deterministic sampled controls derived from this contract, not literature measurements
construction_boundary.historical_profile_roles: all v1-v3 profile contracts remain immutable diagnostics from superseded trap or density choices
construction_boundary.interpretation: The Trap III finite-temperature calculation fixes the shared condensate number and transverse scale. The analytic axial factors retain source-informed smooth, connected and separated morphologies on the representative 2.8 um spacing; they are not recalculated ground states at the listed scattering lengths.
